selected_evidence.requirement: Non-interactive SSH using an RSA key
selected_evidence.summary: The 3072-bit RSA key was created with correct permissions; sshd recorded accepted RSA public-key authentication before reboot, and access succeeded again afterward.

selected_evidence.requirement: Pinned server host key rejects unexpected keys without prompting
selected_evidence.summary: Three current server keys were pinned. Effective policy showed strict checking and batch mode; mismatched keys were rejected with exit code 255 both before and after reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel retained
selected_evidence.summary: Ubuntu 24.04 and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were identical before and after restart.

Captured a healthy baseline, received native reboot acknowledgement, observed boot ID change from f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3 to c8e161de-d74f-457e-818d-8ea12431b617, and verified recovered SSH services, listener, account data, pins, and login.

commands.command:
set -eu
printf 'effective_client_policy:\n'
sudo -u opsadmin -- ssh -G local-node1 | grep -E '^(hostname|user |batchmode|passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication|stricthostkeychecking|checkhostip|updatehostkeys|identityfile|userknownhostsfile|globalknownhostsfile) '

set +e

set -e
printf 'mismatch_rc=%s\n' "$mismatch_rc"
printf '%s\n' "$mismatch_output" | grep -E 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED|Host key verification failed'
test "$mismatch_rc" -ne 0
